raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stacked on #44339 (`hicache/backup-drop-visibility`): this branch is based on it and the PR base points at it, so the diff shown here is the throttle alone. Rebase onto `main` once #44339 lands.

## Motivation

With `--hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only` and `write_through`, a store that drains slower than prefill produces KV loses whole prompts from L3: a finished node's backup intent is queued unpinned until its D2H launches, host staging is held until the storage ack, and `flush_pending_writes` stops launching at `live_cap`, so the device LRU evicts exactly the queued leaves and the stale sweep retires them (`source_evicted` after #44339). The loss is bandwidth-bound: lost ~= produced - (staging window + drain x burst). Re-ordering the eviction walk or pinning queued nodes does not change those terms (pinning turns the device pool into a write buffer for the store's drain time), and back-pressure never reaches admission, so a slow store shows up as a silently collapsing L3 hit rate while TTFT stays flat. Deployments that would rather pay TTFT than lose coverage have no knob.

## Modifications

- **Knob.** `"write_backlog_throttle": true` in `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config` (default `false`; parsed next to `prefetch_threshold` / `prefetch_timeout_*` in `HybridCacheController.parse_storage_backend_extra_config`, type-checked, applied at startup and on runtime attach). It lives with the other storage-controller policy keys rather than a new server arg because it only means something with a storage backend in buffer-only mode.
- **Hold.** `BufferModePipeline.write_backlog_hold_tokens()` is the queued-but-unstaged backlog (`write_backlog_tokens_`, unique spans across pools) while the throttle is on and the write path is alive; `BasePrefixCache.write_backlog_hold_tokens()` (default 0) exposes it and `PrefillAdder.__init__` charges it to `total_offset` / `current_offset`, so prefill admits only what free or already-written device memory can hold and recovers as writes stage. It is a budget charge, not a lock: the eviction walk is unchanged, in-flight chunked prefills and decode growth still evict queued spans (labeled drops), priority preemption still works against the hold, and a stale-swept span releases its share. There is no admission floor: with a live store, sustained admission equals the staging launch rate, which the window caps at the store's drain.
- **Why the whole backlog and not a cap.** A cap at `pool - max_request` (the obvious wedge guard) does not pace: once the backlog exceeds it, each admission evicts the spans it then re-queues, so admission runs at full speed with drops (measured: 45% dropped with a 49k cap on a 65k pool at 0.3 GB/s, same as control; 16% with the real `pool - max_request` at the stock backend). Holding only while the running batch is non-empty degenerates to the cap in prefill-heavy traffic (the running batch is empty between prefill passes), i.e. exactly the PD-prefill shape this is for.
- **Safety from liveness, rank-agreed.** `write_path_alive()` is each rank's verdict: a write launch or storage ack within `write_backlog_stall_timeout_s` (30 s, a class constant), or no backlog at all; stalled latches until the next launch or ack, so a dead store with a held window stays lapsed across sweeps and new backlogs instead of re-arming every timeout (a new backlog only restarts the clock when nothing is staged or in flight). The verdict rides the existing per-tick HiCache MIN all-reduce (`_sync_hicache_ready_counts`); in buffer-only PP the slot is additionally `_pp_sync`'d from PP0 because every stage schedules on its own clock. `set_write_path_alive(False)` lapses the hold with one WARNING and admission proceeds (drops labeled); progress re-engages it (INFO). The storage slots of the sync vector are now derived from one slot list (`_STORAGE_QUEUE_SLOTS`, extra pools, `write_path_alive` last), the PP placeholder from the same count, with a CPU test that placeholder and live lengths match. Slot order to coordinate with #44342: `[..., *extra_pools, write_path_alive, storage_healthy]` keeps its `[-1]` parse valid. The bit is not added to `drain_storage_control_queues` (no callers under `python/sglang/srt`).
- **Scheduler latch.** A NO_TOKEN with a non-empty running batch sets `batch_is_full`, which only a finished or retracted request cleared, so a hold-induced NO_TOKEN would have shut admission until the longest in-flight decode ended. `Scheduler` now records `write_backlog_hold_tokens()` at that NO_TOKEN and reopens admission at the top of `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` once the hold has shrunk below it (one compare per pass; memory-bound NO_TOKENs keep the stock behavior).
- **Docs.** `hicache_design.mdx`: the controller-consumed extra-config keys get their own paragraph; `write_backlog_throttle` says who should turn it on (coverage-first deployments behind slow or remote stores, e.g. PD prefill engines), who should not (latency tiers; anywhere the store drains faster than prefill), that every request queued behind the throttle pays, and the 30 s stall constant.
- **Tests.** `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_buffer_mode_backlog_throttle.py` (CPU: default off holds nothing; the hold is the whole backlog and is released as intents stage or sweep; a stalled write path lapses the hold, stays latched through a sweep and a new backlog while the window is held, re-engages on a storage ack, restarts the clock only when idle; the extra-config key is consumed and type-checked), `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_write_backlog_latch.py` (CPU: the latch reopens when the hold shrinks and holds otherwise, through the real `_get_new_batch_prefill_raw` gate), `test_prefill_adder.py::test_write_backlog_hold_is_charged_to_both_budgets`, `test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py` (PP0's liveness slot is `_pp_sync`'d in buffer-only PP; cache-mode placeholder length equals the live layout), `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py::test_buffer_only_write_backlog_throttle_holds_queued_writes_until_staged` (real cache + file backend across the suite's configs, on and off, including the stall release through `check_hicache_events`).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable (admission pacing only; nothing changes in what is written, read or restored). The GPU runs below verify byte-identical greedy output cold vs L3 on the verify prompts.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Lane: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct TP2 (B200), page 64, `--max-total-tokens 65536 --hicache-ratio 2` (host 131,136 tokens, write window 118,023), python tree core, `HybridCacheController`, `--hicache-storage-backend file`, `buffer_only`, `write_through`, prefetch policy `timeout`; 40 cold prompts x 6-12k tokens, flush, verify, replay with a 64-token extension; per-rank counters (ranks identical). The stock `HiCacheFile` drains at ~1.6 GB/s/rank against ~4.3 GB/s/rank of prefill KV, so every seed overruns the window. All drops are `source_evicted`; the other four reasons stayed 0.

| throttle | conc | seed tokens | dropped / rank | drop % | replay full / zero / partial | seed wall (s) | seed TTFT p50 / p90 / max (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | 8 | 375,192 | 70,592 | 18.8% | 31 / 5 / 4 | 1.25 | 0.222 / 0.259 / 0.345 |
| on | 8 | 369,304 | 22,656 | 6.1% | 36 / 2 / 2 | 1.88 | 0.230 / 0.544 / 0.714 |
| on (seed 2) | 8 | 357,976 | 15,360 | 4.3% | 37 / 1 / 2 | 1.74 | 0.221 / 0.433 / 0.738 |
| on | 4 | 352,664 | 39,744 | 11.3% | 35 / 4 / 1 | 1.35 | 0.086 / 0.151 / 0.225 |

Earlier samples of the same code path at c4/c8 (before the squash) sit in the same bands: off 22-33% at c8 and 22-23% at c4; on 2.6-7.1% at c8 and 7-19% at c4.

Sustained back-pressure (store throttled to 0.3 GB/s with a fault-injecting `HiCacheFile` subclass; c8 seed plus a 256-token never-cached canary every 0.5 s for 70 s):

| throttle | dropped / rank | drop % | replay full / zero / partial | seed wall (s) | seed TTFT p50 / p90 / max (s) | canary TTFT p50 / p90 / p99 (s), >1 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | 160,768 | 44.9% | 22 / 16 / 2 | 1.21 | 0.213 / 0.257 / 0.339 | 0.014 / 0.021 / 0.189, 0 of 140 |
| on | 35,520 | 9.6% | 35 / 3 / 2 | 9.55 | 0.333 / 4.286 / 5.183 | 0.014 / 1.676 / 4.301, 16 of 140 |

Dead store (the first storage `set` hangs forever, so the single backup thread never acks again; c8 seed plus canaries for 120 s, throttle on): exactly one `write backlog throttle released` line per rank, 32 s after the seed started; no re-engage line (the latch holds); canary TTFT p50 15.4 s / max 29.9 s during the 30 s hold, p50 14 ms / p90 18 ms afterwards; all drops labeled `source_evicted`; no other WARNING/ERROR.

Reading: with the throttle on, the seed is paced to the store (9.6 s instead of 1.2 s at 0.3 GB/s), coverage goes from 22 to 35 full replays, and the cost lands on TTFT of everything queued behind the throttled admission, including unrelated short requests. That is the intended trade and why it is opt-in. Under a dead store the price is one stall of the timeout length, then admission with labeled drops.

Validation run (from the repo root, GPU index set for `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`):
- `pytest test_buffer_mode_backlog_throttle.py managers/test_scheduler_write_backlog_latch.py managers/test_prefill_adder.py test_prefill_memory_budget.py test_buffer_mode_sidecar.py test_buffer_mode_backup_drops.py test_storage_prefetch_lifecycle.py observability/test_stat_loggers_di.py test_hicache_pp_sync_drain.py` -> 122 passed.
- `pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py -k "buffer or backup or staged"` (1 GPU) -> 278 passed, 329 skipped (the new case on 13 configs, on + off; Mamba configs skipped by the buffer fixture).
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` -> passed.
- Not run: full CI, AMD/NPU lanes, PP > 1 live (the sync-vector change is covered on CPU), the Rust tree core under the new suite case.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -214,3 +214,7 @@ Specifically, **LMCache**, an efficient KV cache layer for enterprise-scale LLM
 - **`--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config HICACHE_STORAGE_BACKEND_EXTRA_CONFIG`**: the extra config can be either
   - a JSON string containing extra configuration for the storage backend, e.g., `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"prefetch_threshold":512, "prefetch_timeout_base": 0.5, "prefetch_timeout_per_ki_token": 0.25}' `, or
   - a TOML or JSON or YAML file specifying the extra configuration for the storage backend (to differentiate from the JSON string input, prepend a `@` in front of the file name), e.g., `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config "@config.toml"` where `config.toml` is the config file containing the complex configurations. This can be useful when the configuration consists of many or complex key-value pairs (for instance, it is preferred to use a config file for NIXL backend as its configurations can be complex).
+
+  A few keys are consumed by the HiCache controller itself and never reach the backend: `prefetch_threshold`, `prefetch_timeout_base`, `prefetch_timeout_per_ki_token`, `hicache_storage_pass_prefix_keys`, and `write_backlog_throttle`.
+
+  `write_backlog_throttle` (default `false`) only applies with `--hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only`. In that mode a storage backend that drains slower than prefill produces KV loses the queued, not yet staged spans to device eviction (`sglang:hicache_backup_dropped_tokens_total{reason="source_evicted"}`) while TTFT stays flat. With the throttle on, that backlog is withheld from the prefill admission budget, so new admission is paced to the store's drain instead; there is no floor, and every request queued behind the throttle pays, including short unrelated ones (in-flight chunked prefills and decode proceed). Turn it on for coverage-first deployments behind slow or remote stores, for example PD prefill engines; keep it off on latency-sensitive tiers and wherever the store drains faster than prefill. The hold lapses, with a warning, while the write path makes no progress (no write launch or storage ack for 30 s, a fixed constant), so a stalled backend degrades admission but cannot wedge it.

@@ -647,6 +647,12 @@ def __init__(
                     for r in running_batch.reqs
                 ]
             )
+        # Evictable tokens whose L3 write is still queued (buffer-only
+        # throttle): charge them instead of letting admission evict them.
+        write_backlog_hold = tree_cache.write_backlog_hold_tokens()
+        if write_backlog_hold:
+            self.memory_budget.total_offset += write_backlog_hold
+            self.memory_budget.current_offset += write_backlog_hold
 
         # DeepSeek V4 HiSparse wraps an SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator internally and
         # exposes the full SWA allocator interface.

@@ -1291,6 +1291,9 @@ def init_running_status(self):
         self.waiting_queue: List[Req] = []
         # The running decoding batch for continuous batching
         self.running_batch: ScheduleBatch = ScheduleBatch(reqs=[], batch_is_full=False)
+        # Buffer-only write-backlog hold charged when NO_TOKEN last set
+        # batch_is_full; admission reopens once the hold shrinks below it.
+        self._write_backlog_hold_at_full = 0
         # The current forward batch
         self.cur_batch_for_debug: Optional[ScheduleBatch] = None
         # The last forward batch
@@ -3982,6 +3985,16 @@ def _get_new_batch_prefill_raw(
             # An empty batch never reaches update_running_batch, the only
             # other place that clears the flag, so admission would stay shut.
             running_batch.batch_is_full = False
+        if (
+            running_batch.batch_is_full
+            and self._write_backlog_hold_at_full
+            and self.tree_cache.write_backlog_hold_tokens()
+            < self._write_backlog_hold_at_full
+        ):
+            # A hold-induced NO_TOKEN set the flag; staged or swept writes
+            # shrank the hold, so budget may be back before a request finishes.
+            running_batch.batch_is_full = False
+            self._write_backlog_hold_at_full = 0

+"""A NO_TOKEN caused by the buffer-only write-backlog hold must not latch
+``batch_is_full`` until a request finishes: admission reopens as soon as the
+hold shrinks (writes staged or swept), which is the recovery the throttle
+promises."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import ScheduleBatch
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestSchedulerWriteBacklogLatch(CustomTestCase):
+    def _scheduler(self, *, hold_tokens: int, hold_at_full: int) -> Scheduler:
+        """Just enough of a Scheduler for the admission gate at the top of
+        _get_new_batch_prefill_raw; an empty waiting queue returns right after
+        the gate, so the flag's value afterwards is the gate's verdict."""
+        scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+        scheduler.grammar_manager = SimpleNamespace(has_waiting_grammars=lambda: False)
+        scheduler.enable_priority_preemption = False
+        scheduler.is_hybrid_swa = False
+        scheduler.chunked_req = None
+        scheduler.waiting_queue = []
+        scheduler.tree_cache = MagicMock()
+        scheduler.tree_cache.write_backlog_hold_tokens.return_value = hold_tokens
+        scheduler._write_backlog_hold_at_full = hold_at_full
+        return scheduler
+
+    def _running_batch(self) -> ScheduleBatch:
+        return ScheduleBatch(reqs=[MagicMock()], batch_is_full=True)
+
+    def test_flag_clears_once_the_hold_shrinks(self):
+        scheduler = self._scheduler(hold_tokens=30, hold_at_full=40)
+        batch = self._running_batch()
+        self.assertEqual(
+            scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw(None, batch), (None, batch)
+        )
+        self.assertFalse(batch.batch_is_full)
+        self.assertEqual(scheduler._write_backlog_hold_at_full, 0)
+
+    def test_flag_holds_while_the_hold_has_not_shrunk(self):
+        for hold_tokens, hold_at_full in ((40, 40), (50, 40), (0, 0), (40, 0)):
+            with self.subTest(hold_tokens=hold_tokens, hold_at_full=hold_at_full):
+                scheduler = self._scheduler(
+                    hold_tokens=hold_tokens, hold_at_full=hold_at_full
+                )
+                batch = self._running_batch()
+                scheduler._get_new_batch_prefill_raw(None, batch)
+                # Memory-bound NO_TOKENs (hold_at_full == 0) keep the stock
+                # latch: only a finished or retracted request reopens them.
+                self.assertTrue(batch.batch_is_full)
+                self.assertEqual(scheduler._write_backlog_hold_at_full, hold_at_full)
+

+    unittest.main()

+        self.assertEqual(pipeline.write_backlog_hold_tokens(), tokens)

+        del self.states[2]

+        self.assertEqual(pipeline.write_backlog_hold_tokens(), 0)

+    def test_hold_lapses_while_the_write_path_is_stalled(self):
+        """A store that neither launches nor acks within the stall timeout
+        must not keep admission blocked: the local verdict latches stalled,
+        the rank-agreed flag releases the hold, and only a launch or an ack
+        re-engages it. A dead store with a held window must stay lapsed
+        across sweeps and new backlogs instead of re-arming every timeout."""
+        pipeline = self._make_pipeline(throttle=True)
+        # Twelve tokens fill the write window once loads occupy the host pool.
+        self._add_node(1, pages=6)
+        pipeline.enqueue_backup_intent(1)
+        self.assertTrue(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        self._age_past_timeout(pipeline)
+        self.assertFalse(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        with self.assertLogs(pipeline_module.logger, level=logging.WARNING):
+            pipeline.set_write_path_alive(False)
+        self.assertEqual(pipeline.write_backlog_hold_tokens(), 0)
+
+        # A launch is progress: the local verdict recovers and the agreed
+        # flag re-engages the hold for whatever is still queued.
+        self._add_node(2)
+        pipeline.enqueue_backup_intent(2)
+        pipeline._cache.cache_controller.prefetch_tokens_occupied = HOST_POOL_TOKENS
+        pipeline.flush_pending_writes()
+        self.assertEqual(len(pipeline.pending_write_queue), 1)
+        self.assertTrue(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        pipeline.set_write_path_alive(True)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            pipeline.write_backlog_hold_tokens(), pipeline.write_backlog_tokens_
+        )
+        self.assertGreater(pipeline.write_backlog_hold_tokens(), 0)
+
+        # Dead store from here: the launched write never acks. Stalled latches
+        # through the sweep that empties the queue and through a new backlog
+        # (the window is still held, so a new backlog is not a fresh start).
+        self._age_past_timeout(pipeline)
+        self.assertFalse(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        pipeline.set_write_path_alive(False)
+        del self.states[2]
+        del self.snapshots[2]
+        pipeline.flush_pending_writes()
+        self.assertFalse(pipeline.pending_write_queue)
+        self.assertFalse(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        self._add_node(3)
+        pipeline.enqueue_backup_intent(3)
+        self.assertFalse(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        self.assertEqual(pipeline.write_backlog_hold_tokens(), 0)
+        # The storage ack is the progress that clears the latch.
+        (ack_id,) = pipeline.ongoing_write_through
+        pipeline.finish_backup_ack(ack_id)
+        self.assertFalse(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        (operation_id,) = pipeline.ongoing_backup
+        pipeline.finish_storage_write_ack(operation_id)
+        self.assertTrue(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        pipeline.set_write_path_alive(True)
+        self.assertGreater(pipeline.write_backlog_hold_tokens(), 0)

+        # flight the next backlog starts the timeout afresh.
+        pipeline.pending_write_queue.clear()
+        self._age_past_timeout(pipeline)
+        self.assertTrue(pipeline.write_path_alive())
+        self._add_node(4)
+        pipeline.enqueue_backup_intent(4)
+        self.assertTrue(pipeline.write_path_alive())
